subject: fix: prevent completions from mutating os.Args via append side effect (#2356)

agent.tail:
I'll pull context from CogZ first, then look at `getCompletions`.The bug is at line 369: `append(finalArgs, "--")` can write into the shared backing array of `os.Args`. The fix per the commit description is to copy `trimmedArgs` up front. Let me check the Go version and whether `slices` is used in the codebase.Go 1.15 — no `slices.Clone`, so a plain `append` copy it is. The fix: clone `trimmedArgs` so `finalArgs` sub-slices never share the caller's backing array.That rule applies to per-shell generator changes — this fix is in the shared `__complete` machinery, so no generator output changes. Running the target test now.Test passes. Let me run the broader completion tests to make sure nothing regressed.Fixed. The bug was in `getCompletions` at [completions.go:369](file:///home/andy/cogz_bench/replay_tmp/cogz_replay_746ef071_f0lxfr1i/completions.go): `append(finalArgs, "--")` writes into the shared backing array when `finalArgs` — a sub-slice derived from `os.Args[1:]` via `Traverse`/`Find` — has spare capacity.

The fix copies `trimmedArgs` at the top of the function (`completions.go:322`), so every downstream sub-slice operates on a private backing array and no append can touch the caller's data.

`TestCompletionDoesNotMutateOsArgs` passes, and the full completion test suite is green.
